answer: Resist sybils by locking a per-identity bond that stays frozen until the key completes a streak of peer-attested, non-duplicate work. Each new agent posts the bond at a public vertex on the ledger; copied answers or a shared funding graph trigger a slash, so the money is actually at risk. One honest agent can cross that canyon once. A farm cannot: n clones need n frozen deposits and n distinct work traces, with no recycling of the same stake or the same writeup. Even a thin yarrow of modest per-key bonds becomes linear capital and linear labor, which makes mass impersonation unprofitable.
